g10-economics-ue3-t1.overview: Theory of Production sits inside Theories of Production and Cost. Production and cost are the focus of Unit 3 of Grade 10 Economics in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it develops the theory of production, from the production function to returns to scale. Then it turns to the theory of cost in the short run and the long run. Also it links the product curves to the cost curves. Students will also learn how production and cost shape real-life firm decisions.
objectives: State the short-run and long-run production functions.
Calculate average and marginal product and cost.
Explain the law of diminishing marginal productivity.
Draw and relate the product and cost curves.
g10-economics-ue3-t1.simple:
Theory of Production in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, the production function linking inputs to output.
  • Then short-run production, with total, average, and marginal product, and the law of diminishing marginal productivity.
  • Also the three stages of production.
  • Next, long-run production, isoquants, and their properties.
g10-economics-ue3-t1.detailed:
Theory of Production — the essentials. First, the production function linking inputs to output. Then short-run production, with total, average, and marginal product, and the law of diminishing marginal productivity. Also the three stages of production. Next, long-run production, isoquants, and their properties. Finally, returns to scale and the effect of technology change.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • State the short-run and long-run production functions.
  • Calculate average and marginal product and cost.
  • Explain the law of diminishing marginal productivity.
  • Describe returns to scale.
  • Draw and relate the product and cost curves.
